question.text: As per SEBI regulations, mutual funds must dispatch redemption proceeds to investors within:

answer.text: 10 working days of the redemption request
3 working days of the redemption request
30 working days of the redemption request
15 working days of the redemption request

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI regulations require redemption proceeds to be dispatched within 10 working days of receipt of the redemption request. Dividends must be dispatched within 15 days of declaration. If there is a delay, the AMC must pay the unitholder interest at 15% per annum, and this expense must be borne by the AMC (it cannot be charged to the scheme). The Trap: 3 working days is not the regulatory maximum for redemption proceeds in the checked source — the workbook fixes the maximum at 10 working days. 15 days is the timeline for dividend pay-out, not redemption proceeds. 30 days is well beyond the prescribed limit. Note: The 15% per annum delay-interest obligation falls on the AMC and cannot be passed on to the scheme's investors collectively.
